title: Unbounded quotient-scalar refinement of integral direct image
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ put $R_T=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}(A/\pi^m)_T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], and $S_T=(A/\pi^n)_T$, the constant finite quotient ring sheaf, for a fixed $n\geq1$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D_R(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T})$, $D_S(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{S_T})$ of internal module objects, the derived module pullback and pushforward with their derived adjunction [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and the uncompleted relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Set $D_{n,T}K=K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$, the derived scalar extension of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

For any morphism $f:X\to Y$ write $L_{f,R}\dashv F_{f,R}$ and $L_{f,S}\dashv F_{f,S}$ for these adjunctions. Let $\lambda_f:L_{f,S}D_{n,Y}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{n,X}L_{f,R}$ be the canonical scalar/pullback balancing comparison: on flat-term K-flat representatives its forward map sends $f^{-1}(x\otimes s)$ to $f^{-1}x\otimes f^{-1}s$, using the cartesian coefficient identifications [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Define
$$\rho_{f,n,K}:D_{n,Y}F_{f,R}K\longrightarrow F_{f,S}D_{n,X}K$$
to be the adjunct under $L_{f,S}\dashv F_{f,S}$ of $D_{n,X}(\varepsilon^R_{f,K})\circ\lambda_{f,F_{f,R}K}$.

The transformation $\rho_{f,n}$ is a natural isomorphism on all of $D_R(X)$. It is the quotient-scalar refinement of the specified perfect-coefficient projection morphism [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula]: under the internal-module/section-module equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] and restriction $V_T:D(S_T)\to D(R_T)$, the composite
$$V_YD_{n,Y}F_{f,R}K\xrightarrow{V_Y\rho_{f,n,K}}V_YF_{f,S}D_{n,X}K\xrightarrow{d_f}F_{f,R}V_XD_{n,X}K$$
is exactly that projection morphism, where $d_f$ is the derived pushforward/restriction composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. The quotient $S_T$ is resolved by $[R_T\xrightarrow{\pi^n}R_T]$ in degrees $-1,0$, augmented by the actual finite projection $R_T\to S_T$. No properness, completeness, boundedness or constructibility condition on $f$ or $K$ is imposed. For $n\geq m\geq1$, these isomorphisms commute with reduction $A/\pi^n\to A/\pi^m$, using the canonical balanced identifications $(K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_{n,T})\otimes^L_{S_{n,T}}S_{m,T}\simeq K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_{m,T}$ and the corresponding scalar/direct-image mate. Here $S_{j,T}=(A/\pi^j)_T$ for each positive $j$.

source.place: Paragraph (1), the cone-of-uniformizer reduction comparison, with its quotient scalar action and canonical adjunction normalization; original ten-step proof steps 1 and 3. Stacks sites-modules.tex, Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat); sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition). The comparison with internal module objects and the normalization of the quotient-scalar mate are the extracted argument, not a verbatim single Stacks theorem.

proof.text: First identify the actual quotient and its resolution, for every positive integer $j$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a discrete valuation domain; in particular it is Noetherian and $\pi^j\ne0$. The two-term free $A$-complex $[A\xrightarrow{\pi^j}A]$ resolves $A/\pi^j$. The quotients are finite by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients]. The completed coefficient sheaf $R_T$ is the inverse limit of these constant quotients by [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] with $I=(\pi)$: $R_T$ is flat over the constant sheaf $\underline A$, and scalar extension of that finite free resolution is augmented to $S_{j,T}$ by the canonical finite projection. Consequently $R_T/\pi^jR_T\cong S_{j,T}$ with that projection, rather than an arbitrarily chosen quotient isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-scalar-cyclic-resolution] with $a=\pi^j$: multiplication is injective and $[R_T\xrightarrow{\pi^j}R_T]$, in degrees $-1,0$, is a K-flat resolution of $S_{j,T}$. This proves the resolution assertion and supplies perfect coefficient complexes at every level.

proof.text: Work temporarily with section-ring module sheaves. The exact equivalences of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] identify the internal relative tensors, total tensor complexes and K-flat representatives with their section-module versions. Thus they also identify derived scalar extension: on a flat-term K-flat representative $P$, both are the complex $P\otimes_{R_T}S_{j,T}$, by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The unbounded functor and adjunction comparisons of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] identify the specified internal $L_f\dashv F_f$, including their counits, with the ringed-topos ones. Apply this separately to the integral condensed coefficient ring and the discrete finite quotient. Both coefficient identifications are cartesian by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], and they commute with the finite projection, since all maps are pulled back from the point. Apply the normalized derived pullback composition comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to the two paths from $(X,S_{j,X})$ to $(Y,R_Y)$, through $(Y,S_{j,Y})$ and through $(X,R_X)$. They give $\lambda_{f,j}:L_{f,S_j}D_{j,Y}\cong D_{j,X}L_{f,R}$. Its flat-term formula is exactly the balancing map in the statement. These comparisons and the counit are natural, so taking their adjunct defines the specified natural transformation $\rho_{f,j}$.

source.place: Tags 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat; 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; 07A6, lemma-adjoint. Internal/section transport uses the cited comparison statements.

proof.text:
Record the balancing identity needed to identify the map, not merely its endpoints. Suppress $j$ and set $M=F_{f,R}K$. Write $b:V_XL_{f,S}\cong L_{f,R}V_Y$ for the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Under $V_TD_TN=N\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$, the composite
$$L_{f,R}(M\otimes^L S_Y)\xrightarrow{b^{-1}}V_XL_{f,S}D_YM\xrightarrow{V_X\lambda_{f,M}}V_XD_XL_{f,R}M$$
is the canonical tensor comparison $L_{f,R}(M\otimes^LS_Y)\to L_{f,R}M\otimes^LS_X$. Indeed the first arrow regards inverse image of the scalar-extended module as an $S_X$-module; the second sends the inverse image of $x\otimes s$ to $f^{-1}x\otimes f^{-1}s$. This is precisely the pullback-tensor map, with $L_{f,R}S_Y\cong S_X$ from step 1 and the cartesian coefficient identification. The K-flat computation and coherence in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] make this equality valid in the unbounded derived category, independently of representatives. The internal/section comparison used in step 2 preserves these same pure-tensor maps.

source.place: Tags 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition. Explicit specialization of their normalized balancing maps.

proof.text:
Now apply the adjunction-compatibility clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] to $t=D_X(\varepsilon^R_{f,K})\lambda_{f,M}$, whose $S$-adjunct is $\rho_{f,j,K}$. It says that the $R$-adjunct of
$$V_X(t)\circ b^{-1}:L_{f,R}V_YD_YM\longrightarrow V_XD_XK$$
is exactly $d_f\circ V_Y\rho_{f,j,K}$. By step 3 and the K-flat description of derived scalar extension, this first morphism is
$$L_{f,R}(M\otimes^LS_Y)\longrightarrow L_{f,R}M\otimes^LS_X\xrightarrow{\varepsilon^R_{f,K}\otimes1}K\otimes^LS_X.$$
The definition [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map] identifies its adjunct with the specified projection morphism $\pi_{f,K,S_Y}$. Uniqueness in the adjunction therefore gives $d_f V_Y\rho_{f,j,K}=\pi_{f,K,S_Y}$. All identifications are the internal/section and tensor identifications already fixed in steps 2 and 3. In particular this equality uses compatibility of the independently specified adjunctions; it does not infer equality of quotient-linear morphisms from equality after forgetting scalars.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] to $(A,I)=(\mathcal O_E,(\pi))$. Its hypotheses hold: $A$ is commutative Noetherian, all $A/\pi^j$ are finite (hence additively torsion), and all are perfect over $A$ by the two-term free resolutions of step 1. Its completed coefficient sheaves are exactly $R_X,R_Y$, and its finite quotient sheaves are $S_{j,X},S_{j,Y}$. It asserts that the precise $\pi_{f,K,S_{j,Y}}$ of step 4 is invertible for every $K$ in the ordinary unbounded category. Since $d_f$ is an isomorphism, step 4 makes $V_Y\rho_{f,j,K}$ invertible. Restriction reflects isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]; hence $\rho_{f,j,K}$ is invertible in $D(S_{j,Y})$. This proves the claimed natural isomorphism without any condition on $f$ or on the cohomological range of $K$.

source.place: Tag 0944, lemma-projection-formula; Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition. The two-term coefficient resolution is the cone-of-uniformizer argument of blueprint paragraph (1).

proof.text:
Finally fix $n\geq m\geq1$, put $E_T=-\otimes^L_{S_{n,T}}S_{m,T}$, and write $\beta_T:E_TD_{n,T}\cong D_{m,T}$. Use exactly [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]: on representatives $\beta_T$ sends $(x\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $x\otimes\bar s t$ and identifies the composite scalar units with the unit for $R_T\to S_{m,T}$. Let $\lambda^{n,m}:L_{f,S_m}E_Y\cong E_XL_{f,S_n}$ be the pullback balancing comparison and let $\sigma:E_YF_{f,S_n}\to F_{f,S_m}E_X$ be its mate. The normalized composition coherence of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] identifies the pasted square $(E_X\lambda_{f,n})\circ(\lambda^{n,m}D_{n,Y})$ with $\lambda_{f,m}$ under $\beta_Y,\beta_X$: both balanced maps send the inverse image of $(x\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $f^{-1}x\otimes f^{-1}(\bar s t)$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] now gives the equality in $D(S_{m,Y})$
$$\rho_{f,m,K}\circ\beta_{Y,F_{f,R}K}=F_{f,S_m}(\beta_{X,K})\circ\sigma_{D_{n,X}K}\circ E_Y(\rho_{f,n,K}).$$
This is the required reduction compatibility retaining the quotient scalar action. The scalar-unit normalization also identifies the corresponding reduction-unit maps: take their transposes using [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], whose unit is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. No flatness of $S_n\to S_m$ is used. In particular the argument does not claim that $S_m$ is perfect over $S_n$ or that $\sigma$ is invertible on arbitrary inputs. For $n=m$ all balancing maps and scalar units are identities, giving the identity compatibility.

The statement is true: after forgetting scalars ρ is the projection map with the K-flat [R→π^n R] resolution, i.e. the cone of π^n. Edge cases f=id, n=m, K=0 and n>m pass, and the proof correctly avoids a regular resolution of S_m over S_n. Step 1 is checked against Stacks 093M (sites-modules.tex l.8261): via completed-constant-sheaf-reduction and flat-scalar-cyclic-resolution the canonical projection gives R/π^j≅S_j, and O_E is a Noetherian DVR. Step 2: internal and section tensor and pushpull (counits included) are identified, cartesian coefficients are untwisted, and λ is the c_{f,g} comparison of the two factorizations. Step 3: since pullbacks are the exact f^{-1} lifts, r(λ)b^{-1} is the tensor comparison. Step 4: the adjunction-compatibility clause of lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction gives d∘r(ρ) = adjunct of (ε⊗1)∘c = π_{f,K,S_Y}, matching def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map and Stacks 0B56 (l.13666). Step 5: the perfect projection formula holds for (O_E,(π)) (Noetherian, k_E finite torsion, P_n finite and perfect), for unbounded K; d is invertible and restriction reflects isomorphisms. Step 6: β normalization plus mate-pasting clause (1), with the elementary naturality of mates under the invertible β; units normalize as x↦x⊗1.
